description: Which of the 5 ICA profiles the customer matches (1-5)
detection_method: Derived from FFG settlement data: loan type, loan amount, age, employment type. POLR applies ICA rules at settlement. Can be overridden manually by broker.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to ICA 5 (Prime Vehicle) as most common mid-range profile. Flag for manual review by broker at Month 3 touchpoint.
notes: ICA assignment is algorithmic but imperfect. Broker override is important for edge cases. FHL-only customers get ICA assigned at cross-sell qualification.

description: Whether the customer owns property (yes/no/unknown)
detection_method: Asked during qualification call, application form, or Month 1 settlement call. For FHL customers, inherent (they are buying or refinancing property). For FFG customers, must be explicitly captured.
fallback_if_unknown: Set to 'unknown'. Block FHL cross-sell content until confirmed. Create qualification task for next broker touchpoint. This is the #1 priority data gap to close.
data_gap_detail: FFG does NOT currently capture homeowner status at entry or during application. This is the single biggest blocker for cross-sell routing. Without it, POLR cannot determine if an FFG customer is FHL-eligible. MUST be added to FFG intake process.
notes: FHL customers are inherently homeowners (or becoming homeowners). The gap is FFG-side only.

description: Which Fox businesses the customer has a relationship with (ffg/fhl/umi/none/combination)
detection_method: POLR record lookup by email or phone at entry. Cross-references all three business databases. Deduplication logic matches on email (primary), phone (secondary), name+DOB (tertiary).
fallback_if_unknown: Treat as new customer (no existing relationship). POLR deduplication runs async — if match found later, merge records and update states.
data_gap_detail: Currently no unified database across FFG/FHL/UMI. POLR will be the unified layer but until built, cross-referencing is manual. Ambition (FFG) has API for real-time lookup. Finshaw's (FHL) is CSV-only with weekly lag. UMI LMS access unknown.
notes: POLR's unified identity is the solution. Pre-POLR, this requires manual checking by brokers.

description: Employment classification (payg/self_employed/contractor/business_owner)
detection_method: Captured in loan application (both FFG and FHL). FFG data available via Ambition API. FHL data via Finshaw's CSV export. Also available from application documents.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to PAYG (most common). Flag for confirmation at next touchpoint.
notes: Employment type is well-captured in both LMS systems as it's required for loan assessment. Key differentiator for ICA 4 (Business Asset Borrower).

description: FHL customer's property purchase type (fhb/new_purchase/refinance/investor/commercial)
detection_method: Captured at FHL application. Defines which FHL lifecycle content they receive (segmented at Month 3 Confidence Pack). Extracted from Finshaw's CSV export.
fallback_if_unknown: Ask Bill Robb directly. This should never be unknown for an FHL customer — it's fundamental to the loan application.
notes: FHL Purchase Type drives ICA routing (Matrix 3) and lifecycle content personalisation (Matrix 5). Journey-based: FHB stays FHB until 2nd property.

description: Household structure (single/couple/family_with_children/shared/with_parents)
detection_method: Partially captured in loan applications (dependants count). Full picture requires self-declaration during qualification or lifecycle touchpoints. Life events (baby, marriage) detected via check-in calls.
fallback_if_unknown: Omit household-specific personalisation. Use generic lifecycle content. Capture at next human touchpoint.
data_gap_detail: Loan applications capture dependants count but not full household picture. Not critical for cross-sell routing but useful for content personalisation and life event detection.
notes: Becomes more important over time as life events drive finance needs. Month 12 Annual Review is a natural capture point.

description: FFG loan product type (motor_vehicle/personal_loan/equipment/fleet/commercial_vehicle/caravan_boat)
detection_method: Captured at FFG application and settlement. Available via Ambition API in real-time. Directly informs ICA assignment.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown — it's the core of the FFG loan record.
notes: Primary input for ICA assignment algorithm. Motor vehicle (used, sub-$30K) = ICA 1. Equipment/fleet = ICA 4. Motor vehicle (new, $40K+) = ICA 5.

description: FFG loan amount in AUD
detection_method: Settlement data from Ambition. Real-time via API.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
notes: Loan amount is a key ICA differentiator. Sub-$30K = likely ICA 1. $40K+ = likely ICA 5. $50K+ equipment = likely ICA 4.

description: FHL loan amount in AUD
detection_method: Settlement data from Finshaw's. CSV export only — weekly lag.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
notes: Average FHL loan amount is ~$600K. Used for equity calculations, LVR tracking, and refinance pathway analysis.

description: FFG loan term in months
detection_method: Settlement data from Ambition API.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to 60 months (5 years, most common for asset finance).
notes: Used to calculate balloon payment dates, end-of-term triggers, and renewal opportunities.

description: FFG lending institution
detection_method: Settlement data from Ambition API.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
notes: Relevant for early payout processes (Doc 11 has 30+ lender payout procedures). Required when customer requests early payout.

description: FHL lending institution
detection_method: Settlement data from Finshaw's CSV export.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
notes: Required for rate repricing negotiations (Month 6), fixed rate expiry tracking, and refinance pathway analysis (Month 15).

description: Current FHL interest rate (fixed or variable)
detection_method: Settlement data and periodic updates from Finshaw's CSV export.
fallback_if_unknown: Ask Bill Robb directly. Critical for Month 6 Pricing Review.
notes: Rate type (fixed vs variable) determines whether fixed_rate_expiry is relevant. Variable rate customers get different Month 15 content.

description: Date FFG loan settled
detection_method: Settlement event from Ambition API. Real-time.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
notes: Anchors the entire FFG lifecycle. All lifecycle month calculations derive from this date.

description: Date FHL loan settled
detection_method: Settlement data from Finshaw's CSV export. Weekly lag.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown.
data_gap_detail: Finshaw's CSV export has a weekly lag. A loan that settles on Monday may not appear in POLR until the following week's export. This delays FHL lifecycle Month 1 welcome sequence. Workaround: Bill or Paige manually updates POLR on settlement day.
notes: The weekly lag from Finshaw's is a known constraint. Manual entry is the stopgap until a better integration exists.

description: Date the FHL customer's fixed interest rate period ends
detection_method: Captured at settlement for fixed-rate loans. Extracted from Finshaw's CSV.
fallback_if_unknown: For fixed-rate customers, this MUST be captured. If missing, Bill Robb must source from lender directly. For variable-rate customers, this field is not applicable.
notes: Drives the 90-day fixed rate expiry trigger (Matrix 2 handoff ho-trigger-fixed-rate-expiry). One of the strongest retention and cross-sell triggers.

description: Date of balloon payment on FFG loan (if applicable)
detection_method: Captured at FFG settlement for balloon-structured loans. Available via Ambition API.
fallback_if_unknown: For balloon loans, this MUST be captured. If missing, calculate from settlement date + loan term. For non-balloon loans, not applicable.
notes: Drives the 90-day balloon payment trigger (Matrix 2 handoff ho-trigger-balloon-payment). Customer decision point: refinance, trade up, or pay out.

description: Expected end date of FFG loan (final repayment or balloon)
detection_method: Calculated from settlement_date_ffg + loan_term_ffg. Or captured directly from Ambition API.
fallback_if_unknown: Calculate from settlement date + term.
notes: Drives the end-of-term re-engagement touchpoint (FFG lifecycle Month 18-24). Important for repeat business pipeline.

description: Predicted next product or service the customer will need
detection_method: Derived from ICA profile + lifecycle stage + homeowner status + engagement signals. POLR algorithm combines multiple signals: ICA 3 (repeat) likely needs new vehicle in 2-3 years. ICA 4 (business) likely needs more equipment as business grows. Homeowner + no FHL = refinance or new purchase candidate.
fallback_if_unknown: Use ICA-default next need (from ICA framework routing_logic). Update when human conversation provides clarity.
notes: This is the AI prediction layer. Starts low reliability and improves as engagement data and human conversations enrich the profile. Brokers can override based on direct customer conversations.

description: Customer engagement with cross-sell content (emails opened, packs downloaded, portal pages visited)
detection_method: POLR portal tracks page views, downloads, and time spent. SendGrid tracks email opens and clicks. Combined into engagement score. Specific content engagement signals cross-sell readiness (e.g., reading FHL content = FHL interest).
fallback_if_unknown: Default engagement_score to 0. Treat as cold until engagement signals are detected. Rely on lifecycle-triggered outreach rather than behaviour-triggered.
notes: Behavioural signals complement lifecycle triggers. A customer who opens the FFG Momentum Pack email and clicks through to the portal is a warmer lead than one who ignores it.

description: Customer use of online borrowing calculators or tools
detection_method: POLR portal or website tracks calculator usage. Captures inputs (loan amount, income, property price). Strong intent signal for specific products.
fallback_if_unknown: No action. Calculator usage is a bonus signal, not a required input.
notes: Future state (post-POLR launch). Existing FFG/FHL customers using calculators on the portal are showing active intent. Immediate routing signal.

description: Customer directly asks about a product or service (phone, email, portal chat)
detection_method: Broker logs in POLR when customer mentions a need. Portal chat or inquiry forms capture direct requests. Strongest intent signal.
fallback_if_unknown: N/A — this is an event, not a persistent variable.
notes: When a customer says 'I need a home loan' or 'I'm thinking about a new car', that's the strongest signal. Must be captured immediately in POLR by the broker.

description: Which businesses the customer is eligible to be cross-sold to (ffg/fhl/both/none)
detection_method: Derived from: existing_fox_relationship + homeowner_status + ica_profile + current lifecycle stage. POLR calculates automatically. Rules: FFG customer + homeowner = FHL eligible. FHL customer = FFG eligible (always, since they have transport/equipment needs). Both settled = none (already cross-sold). Declined in one = check other independently.
fallback_if_unknown: Set to 'unknown'. Resolve by capturing homeowner_status.
notes: This is a derived field, not directly captured. Depends on homeowner_status being known (for FFG→FHL direction). FHL→FFG eligibility is always assumed true.

description: Customer has not engaged with any POLR content, emails, or touchpoints for extended period
detection_method: POLR tracks last_login, last_email_opened, last_touchpoint_response. If no engagement for 60+ days during active lifecycle, flag as churn risk. If no engagement for 90+ days post-lifecycle, flag as dormant.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to no churn risk. Only flag when positive disengagement signals are detected.
notes: Churn risk in financial services means the customer refinances elsewhere or goes to a competitor for their next need. Early detection allows proactive intervention.

description: Signals that customer may be comparing rates or considering competitor offers
detection_method: Indirect signals: customer asks about their current rate, requests payout figure, mentions competitor offer, or stops engaging after receiving rate information. Broker must log these signals in POLR.
fallback_if_unknown: No action. These signals are opportunistic — captured when they happen.
notes: Early payout requests (Doc 11) are a strong churn signal. Proactive pricing review (Month 6) is designed to pre-empt rate shopping.

description: Major life event that changes finance needs (new baby, marriage, divorce, new job, business growth, retirement)
detection_method: Captured during lifecycle touchpoint conversations (Month 12 Annual Review is the primary capture point). Broker logs in POLR. Some events may be inferred from address changes, income changes, or dependant count changes.
fallback_if_unknown: No action. Life events are captured opportunistically. Lifecycle touchpoints (especially Month 12) are designed to surface them.
notes: Life events are the strongest cross-sell triggers. A new baby may trigger FHB need (ICA 1→FHL) or upsizing (FHL refinance). Business growth triggers equipment needs (FHL→FFG ICA 4).

description: Current estimated property value (FHL customers)
detection_method: Cotality API integration provides automated property valuations. First valuation at FHL settlement. Updated at Month 3 (90-Day Confidence Pack), Month 12 (Annual Review), and on-demand. Stored in POLR.
fallback_if_unknown: For FHL customers, use settlement purchase price as baseline until Cotality integration is live. For FFG customers, not applicable unless homeowner (then request from customer or estimate from address).
data_gap_detail: Cotality integration is part of POLR MVP scope but not yet built. Until live, property valuations are manual (Bill estimates or uses free online tools). This reduces the impact of Month 3 Confidence Pack and Month 12 Annual Review.
notes: Property value growth is a key trigger for equity-based cross-sell (investment property, equity release for FFG assets). Cotality integration is critical for automation.

description: Current equity in property (property_value minus loan_balance)
detection_method: Calculated: property_value (Cotality) minus loan_amount_fhl (Finshaw's). Updated when either input changes. Requires both data sources to be current.
fallback_if_unknown: Estimate from settlement LVR and assumed repayment schedule. Flag as estimated in POLR.
data_gap_detail: Depends on both Cotality (not yet integrated) and Finshaw's (weekly CSV lag). Loan balance from Finshaw's may be weeks old. Cotality valuation may not be current. Combined accuracy is lower than either individual source.
notes: Equity position drives Month 9 FFG Momentum Pack messaging (equity release pack), Month 15 Refinance Pathway, and investment property conversations.

description: Rough credit quality indicator (good/fair/poor/unknown)
detection_method: NOT directly captured. Inferred from: loan approval (approved = good+), lender tier (major bank = good, non-bank = fair, UMI = poor), application outcome, and any decline reasons logged.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to 'unknown'. Do not make credit assumptions. Only relevant for UMI→FHL pathway where credit improvement is the trigger.
data_gap_detail: Fox does not have direct access to credit scores. Cannot pull credit files without customer consent for a specific purpose. Inference from loan outcomes is the only option. This limits precision in routing UMI customers to FHL.
notes: Credit score is a regulatory-sensitive area. Do not present inferred credit quality to customers. Internal routing use only.

description: Composite score (0-100) measuring customer engagement with POLR platform and Fox communications
detection_method: POLR calculates from: portal logins, content views, email opens/clicks, touchpoint responses, calculator usage, document downloads. Weighted: portal login (high), email click (medium), email open (low). Updated daily.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to 0. Increases as engagement events are captured. New customers start at 0 and build over time.
notes: Engagement score helps prioritise cross-sell outreach. A customer with score 80 who receives the Momentum Pack is far more likely to convert than one with score 10. Use to prioritise Bill's call list.

description: Date of customer's most recent POLR portal login
detection_method: POLR authentication system logs every login with timestamp.
fallback_if_unknown: null (customer has never logged in). Flag for portal re-engagement at next touchpoint.
notes: Customers who actively use the portal are more engaged and more likely to cross-sell. Customers who never log in may need different channel strategy.

description: How the customer originally came to Fox (direct/referral/dealer/aggregator/cross-sell/portal)
detection_method: Captured at entry (Matrix 1). Stored permanently in POLR. Referral customers get tagged with referrer name and type.
fallback_if_unknown: Default to 'direct'. Tag as 'source_unknown' for later cleanup.
notes: Referral source influences ICA affinity and conversion likelihood. Referral customers convert higher. Dealer leads skew ICA 1 and ICA 5. Aggregator leads are lowest quality.

description: Customer's age (derived from date of birth)
detection_method: Date of birth captured in loan application. Available from Ambition API (FFG) or Finshaw's CSV (FHL). Age calculated dynamically.
fallback_if_unknown: Estimate from other data points. Not critical for routing but important for ICA assignment accuracy.
notes: Age is a primary ICA differentiator. 18-30 = likely ICA 1. 35-50 = likely ICA 2. 30-45 repeat = ICA 3. Used alongside loan type and amount for ICA algorithm.

description: Customer's residential address
detection_method: Captured in loan application. Available from Ambition API (FFG) or Finshaw's CSV (FHL).
fallback_if_unknown: Required for loan application — should never be missing.
notes: Address changes can signal life events (moved house = potential new finance needs). Also used for Cotality property lookup. If address is a rental vs owned property, it indicates homeowner status.

description: Whether the customer has had 2+ loans with Fox (any business)
detection_method: POLR checks loan history across all businesses. If 2+ settled loans found (any combination of FFG/FHL/UMI), flag as repeat customer. Influences ICA assignment (repeat = likely ICA 3).
fallback_if_unknown: Default to first-time until POLR has full history. Pre-POLR, broker knowledge is the source.
data_gap_detail: Until POLR unifies data from Ambition, Finshaw's, and UMI LMS, repeat customer detection across businesses is manual. A customer might be a repeat FFG client but Bill doesn't know they also had an FHL loan 3 years ago.
notes: Cross-business repeat detection is a core POLR value proposition. Currently impossible without manual checking.

description: Record of previous cross-sell attempts and outcomes (offered/interested/declined/converted)
detection_method: POLR logs every cross-sell touchpoint: content delivered, email opened, call made, outcome recorded. Brokers must log call outcomes. Prevents repeat pitching to customers who already declined.
fallback_if_unknown: Treat as no previous attempts. Risk of re-pitching.
notes: Critical for Matrix 4 state resolution. If a customer declined FHL at Month 9, the Month 12 approach is different. If they declined twice, back off entirely. Prevents relationship damage from over-selling.

description: Customer consent for data sharing between Fox businesses and marketing communications
detection_method: Captured at POLR registration or loan application. Granular: consent for FFG marketing, FHL marketing, UMI data sharing, Cotality property lookup. Stored in POLR with timestamp.
fallback_if_unknown: Do NOT cross-sell without consent. If consent is unknown, the customer must be asked before any cross-business data sharing or marketing. Compliance critical.
data_gap_detail: No unified consent framework currently exists across FFG/FHL/UMI. Each business has its own consent mechanisms. POLR needs a unified consent model that covers cross-business data sharing, marketing communications, and Cotality data usage. Must be designed before POLR launch.
notes: Regulatory requirement. FFG→UMI handoff (decline reroute) specifically requires customer consent (noted in Matrix 2 handoff ho-ffg-decline-to-umi). Financial services compliance is strict.

description: Details of the asset financed through FFG (make, model, year, type, value)
detection_method: Captured at FFG application and settlement. Available via Ambition API.
fallback_if_unknown: Should never be unknown — core to FFG loan record.
notes: Asset details inform ICA assignment (used car vs new car vs equipment vs fleet). Also useful for future cross-sell timing (car age = replacement cycle).

description: Whether the FHL loan is fixed rate, variable rate, or split
detection_method: Captured at FHL settlement from Finshaw's data.
fallback_if_unknown: Ask Bill Robb directly.
notes: Fixed rate customers need the fixed_rate_expiry_date trigger. Variable rate customers get different Month 6 Pricing Review content. Split loans need both paths.

description: Loan-to-Value Ratio at FHL settlement
detection_method: Calculated from loan_amount_fhl / property_value at settlement. Captured in Finshaw's data.
fallback_if_unknown: Calculate from loan amount and purchase price.
notes: LVR improvement over time signals equity growth. When LVR drops below 80%, LMI savings become a refinance argument. Below 60% opens investment lending opportunities.

description: Customer has requested early loan payout (FFG)
detection_method: Broker logs in POLR when customer requests payout figure. References Doc 11 (Early Payout Guide) for lender process.
fallback_if_unknown: N/A — this is an event trigger.
notes: STRONG buying signal. Per Doc 11 cross-sell trigger note: customer may be trading up (new FFG loan), refinancing elsewhere (retention risk), received windfall (other needs), or selling asset (life change). Always ask why.
